The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook. However, the FOMC’s rapid move to the effective lower bound, large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repo operations, and coordinated dollar swap lines are consistent with the credit-channel literature (e.g., Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch), which emphasizes that easing financial frictions lowers external finance premia and helps stabilize spending. With market-based inflation compensation falling, the deflation risk identified in monetary theory and empirical VAR evidence (e.g., Sims) supports forceful, countercyclical policy to anchor expectations and dampen output volatility. Net tone: negative on the outlook but partially offset by aggressive policy support.
